facts.text: Joseph Brant Hospital tops Burlington's public sector employers with 2,038 full-time employees, while Sofina Foods, Evertz Microsystems and Cogeco lead private sector employers.
Burlington's leading industrial sectors by employment are food processing, packaging, electronics, motor vehicle and transportation, business services, chemical and pharmaceutical, and environmental.
Over 2,500 new jobs were created in Burlington in 2024, with the largest job sectors being other services, accommodation and food services, and health care and social assistance.
Burlington's business growth rate stands at 7.88 percent from 2018 to 2023, and no single sector dominates its diverse economy.

overview: Burlington had 186,948 residents in the 2021 Census, a 2.0 percent increase from 183,314 in 2016, with 73,180 occupied private dwellings spread over 186.12 square kilometres that include a large rural north. Growth is slow, so the customer base is stable rather than expanding.

The median age of 44.4 is the oldest among the cities profiled here and the median household income was $110,000 in 2020. That describes settled, financially comfortable households, many of them empty nesters and retirees. A local business succeeds by earning trust, offering convenience and staying visible to residents who have lived here for years.
